Subject: SIG follow-up: questions on prompt logs, retention, and training

Hi Laura / team,

Thanks for the initial SIG packet. A few follow-ups from our security review that need clarification before we can move this through procurement:

1) Data retention: what's your default retention for request/response logs and can this be shortened per-customer?
2) Prompt/log storage: are prompts and model outputs stored in cleartext in any long-term storage? Do you use derived embeddings or other transformations for indexing?
3) Training on customer data: do you ever use customer prompt/response pairs to improve models (in-house or with third parties) unless we explicitly opt in?

We'd appreciate clear, short answers we can paste into our SIG matrix + any supporting evidence (SOC 2 section, architecture diagram, or policy).

Thanks,
Samantha

--- DRAFT START ---
Redwood Inference — short answers for Acme:
1) Data retention: Default request/response logs are retained for 90 days. Customers may request shorter retention (minimum 7 days) as a configuration option for Hosted and Dedicated plans; Private deployments are customer-controlled.
2) Prompt/log storage: All request and response payloads are stored encrypted at rest (AES-256) and encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+). Short-lived caches (KV cache) may exist in-memory on serving nodes but are not persisted. We do not index raw prompts in a shared long-term index; optional derived embeddings are available only when explicitly enabled by the customer.
3) Training on customer data: Redwood does not use customer prompts/responses to train our production models unless a customer provides explicit, written opt-in and scope (e.g., data-sharing for model improvement). We provide contractual language and a Data Use Addendum for customers who opt to share data for research/training.

Evidence provided: SOC2 report (attached), SIG response workbook (attached), architecture diagram (link), Data Use Addendum template (link).

--- DRAFT END ---

Vivek, is the 90/7 day guidance correct? If not, tell me and I'll revise. Also adding SOC2 pdf and the Redwood_SIG_Responses_v1.xlsx to the response.

Samantha / Jordan — thanks for the questions. Below are concise answers you can paste into the SIG matrix, followed by attachments and links to our evidence. Let us know if you'd like us to fill the SIG worksheet directly.

1) Data retention
- Default retention: 90 days for request/response logs on Redwood Hosted.
- Customer controls: Customers can request reduced retention down to 7 days for Hosted and Dedicated; Private deployments are under customer control and retention is configurable by the customer.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report (attached), retention policy section in the attached SIG workbook.

2) Prompt/log storage
- Storage: Request and response payloads are stored encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+ / TLS 1.3).
- Indexing: We do not index raw prompts into shared long-term search indexes by default. Customers may opt in to derived services (e.g., embedding indexing) which are explicitly documented and can be disabled per account.
- In-memory caches: KV caches used by the serving runtime are short-lived and not persisted to long-term storage.
- Evidence: Architecture diagram (link inside SIG workbook), sample encryption configuration excerpt (attached workbook).

3) Training on customer data
- Policy: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts, responses, or other customer-provided data to train our public or internal models unless we have explicit, documented, and signed opt-in from the customer (Data Use Addendum).
- Third parties: We do not share customer prompt/response pairs with third-party model trainers without customer consent.
- Evidence: Data Use Addendum template (link in workbook), legal confirmation (SOC 2 / policy references).

Attachments: Redwood_SIG_Responses_v1.xlsx (completed cells + evidence pointers), SOC2-report-2025.pdf (redacted report).

Related links: https://drive.redwood.ai/ACME/stack/SIG-Responses-ACME (architecture diagram, retention excerpts); DocuSign://envelope/0A12B3C4D5 (Data Use Addendum).

If you'd like, we can also supply a short architecture diagram PNG or have one of our engineers join a short call to walk through the flow.
